reviews.review: Possibly the best co-op, roguelike, action, open-world, dungeon raid game made. When you get a whole party of eight, it becomes insane.

Fun, addictive, and lots of potential. I think the game is worth it as is but with a handful of new items, weapons, classes, and quest options, this could go from an 7-8/10 to a 9/10 with ease. 

My biggest suggestions for the dev(s) would be (in no particular order):
1) Loadouts - select different starting weapons and abilities for each class. These could be locked behind achievements or progression from more to works towards.
2) Leveling - each character you play levels up. This doubles as a good way to release character specific unlocks.
3) More quest options - right now there's two quests, more variety would be very welcomed.
4) Then the more obvious stuff - More Classes - More items - More weapons

Greater than the sum of its parts. 
-
Surprised by how good the core gameplay is. Nothing ground breaking, but surprisingly competent for the overall appearance and tone of the game in its current EA state. Purchased because a few of my friends were playing and it's definitely better with a group, but can be enjoyed solo. 
-
If the humor hits for you you'll get a lot of enjoyment out of the game, but beyond the references that cover pretty much every aspect of pop culture the gameplay isn't going to blow you away on its own.
-
The biggest complaint at the moment is that every run feels the same and every character feels the same. This seems like a problem with the stats more than the characters themselves, as there's no reason to get stats beyond your primary and then just choosing a secondary, but even a tertiary will give you a damage boost, so once you're fast enough you just grab everything and get stronger regardless. The "loadout" screen makes me believe this will be worked on more in future patches, but at the moment there just isn't any variety as every character benefits from the same items and stats pretty much equally with few exceptions. 
-
Meta progression is incredibly basic as well. Maybe in the future characters will have individual perk trees or some other system, but at the moment you just buff all your characters with armor, damage, health, etc. It would go a long way to offset the "samey" issue to have the characters have various perks unique to them tied into the meta progression. 
-
All that said, I think the game is good and can only improve, so I recommend it both for the fun you can have now, and that there's a solid game to build more content and systems into.

As of the 0.6 update, 3/5 game with a 4/5 value proposition. 

I think there's a solid foundation here, and the fact that it can go up to 8-player co-op without being a party game is a rare occurrence in the current gaming landscape. It's definitely cool to be able to hold four weapons and switch to each just to use their skill. The setting and charm is there as well (being told "git gud" and "skill issue" on defeat, and extracting in a van held by a crow/raven are just some examples lol). The game is just wacky in general. And for $15, you could easily get a lot of hours thanks to the unique characters and some build variety.

That said, I think there are a couple things I'd like to see addressed in the future:
- There is a TON of map traversal, but it's mostly empty space. Action only really happens at camps. In ROR2, you're constantly dealing with enemies while moving around. In Ravenswatch, you move around a map a lot but there are enemies on the way to camps. In LORT, you only really fight at said camps. Sure, there are "bouncing pads" to help you traverse, but having to run through a bunch of empty space is uninteresting.
- Two of the most important ways to get stronger are just stat bumps. During a run, your most important damage boost comes from attribute increases (STR, AGI, or INT). Outside a run, meta-progression comes down to stat bumps. The most interesting upgrades in many rogue games are ones that are game-changing and build-defining. Stat bumps in general are boring.
- Game balance needs some finetuning. Melee, while definitely viable, doesn't jumpstart or get easier nearly as well as ranged. Movement Speed is KING in a game like this. There's little reason to invest in any stat other than your main one, even with the intro of dual stat weapons. The power gap between white, green, blue and purple artifacts are not as noticeable. Solo/scaling with the different player counts feels off. There are regular enemies that are cake walks and others that will one-shot you. The list goes on.
- There's a general lack of content and variety. You can pick different weapons, but why would you if they don't match your main stat? You can pick different missions, but the maps and bosses are still the same. Granted, I'm sure more will come with future updates.

I'm hopeful to see more, and there is a good game here. And again, you could do much worse for $15. At the same time, I think you can spend your time and attention on other EA rogue games. Or at least, until this one has cooked a little bit more.

Really fun little game. Learning curve can be sharp and you can feel as though it's incomprehensible that you would be able to keep up with the power curve through 5 stages. BUT after a few runs, you really get a feel for it and the rougelike elements really come into play.

It's paced well, provides variety of runs - trying to drag a slow/poor start as far as you can, vs OP runs that are fun and stress free almost from the get-go.

Would recommend playing with friends and learning together.

In short: I love this game. If you love addictive, frenetic action games that you can play solo or with friends, LORT is for you. Friends recommended it because we enjoyed games like Muck and Risk of Rain, and I have to say LORT is in that same vein but I like it even more.

On my first couple of playthroughs, I didn't appreciate the importance of taking down forts to increase attributes. I could squeak by the second level, but I would be comically underpowered by the third level. Once I understood the basic gameplay loop (prioritize attribute upgrades, scooping up power-ups and gold as you're able), I was thoroughly addicted.

It's a silly world with a fun aesthetic. The addictive gameplay loop, character designs, and unlocks keep me coming back, and the quest for "the perfect run" adds endless replayability. I love it solo or with friends -- it's just a good time no matter how you play it.

In my opinion, the speed power-ups are the best: a good run starts with becoming The Flash so you can cover as much ground as possible, scooping up everything on every map. Everything falls into place pretty naturally when you can zip across the map easily, prioritizing whatever attributes/power-ups/weapons best suit your play style.

I've already gotten 100% of the achievements and Rune Juice upgrades, so I can't wait for the next update. Like I said -- I'm addicted (and as is implied, I need to get a life). I hope the developers will continue to support this game: new characters and weapons with less min/max attribute scaling (e.g., a character with weapons that benefit from more distributed attributes) would be interesting, and I'd love to see new maps and higher difficulty options.

Thanks for an awesome game, Big Distraction! Live. Laugh. LORT.

Verdict: LORT is really fun early access and I am excited to see where the game goes from here 

+ Positives +
+ Steam achievements (42, around 50 hours now)
+ Really fun to play 
+ Characters feel unique 
+ Weapons have different sets and weight to them
+ Tons and tons of pickups 
+ Easy to get into 
+ Skins to unlock (basic, for the first win, for 10k kills) 
+ Devs listen to the feedback 

– Negatives –
- No Steam trading cards (as of yet)
- Bugs (enemies may go on a stroll, preventing you from getting camp rewards)
- Really grindy unlocks (50 golden lunchboxes, 50 liutenants, 100 epic powerups)
- Balance is all-over place (some pickups are near useless, some are near auto wins) 
- Multiplayer makes the game really easy
